examples.knowledge_point: Writing the Equation of a Vertical Hyperbola in Standard Form
examples.problem: Write the equation of the hyperbola $4y^2-7x^2=84$ in standard form.
examples.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{y^2}{a^2} - \frac{x^2}{b^2}=1.
$$

Therefore, to write the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to divide both sides of the equation by $84$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}-7{x}^{2} & =84 \\ \frac{4{y}^{2}}{84}-\frac{7{x}^{2}}{84} & =\frac{84}{84} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{21}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{12} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
The equation of the hyperbola $7{x}^{2}-27{y}^{2}=189$ in standard form is{{field-1}}
$=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Therefore, to write the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to divide both sides of the equation by $189$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}7{x}^{2}-27{y}^{2} & =189 \\ \frac{7{x}^{2}}{189}-\frac{27{y}^{2}}{189} & =\frac{189}{189} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{27}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{7} & =1\end{aligned}
$$
